title: betula-cluster: memory-bounded BETULA clustering with a Rust core
description:
Memory-bounded clustering for large embeddings and tabular streams. The data is compressed once into numerically stable BETULA cluster features — a CF-tree whose leaf count is capped, so streaming memory stays flat in N and the summary never loses digits far from the origin the way classic BIRCH does — and the clustering head then runs on that summary rather than on the points: k-means, Gaussian mixtures (diagonal, full, Toeplitz, subspace), Ward, spectral, Leiden community detection, HDBSCAN-style density clustering over microclusters, directional (von Mises-Fisher / Watson / spherical k-means) heads for L2-normalized embeddings, scale-space density modes and a Mapper skeleton. Cost is set by the microcluster count, not by N.

The core is Rust with PyO3 bindings; NumPy is the only runtime dependency, and there is no LAPACK, BLAS or SciPy at run time. Streaming partial_fit, a scikit-learn-compatible API, order-invariant builds, soft assignment, coresets, outliers and representatives. Distributed on PyPI (pip install betula-cluster) and crates.io (cargo add betula-cluster); documentation at ilgrad.github.io/betula-cluster.
